title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 11 board. The Eddies made it eight straight behind Brock Purdy's 55 in his first week and sit alone in first at 8-2, Doubtpfizer dropped 341.5 and won by a record 162, the Dongers scored 289.5 and lost, and the SPD's won and still got thrown off the bus, leaving four riders. Substation beat LAB on Last Ride, so LAB is out for good, and eight teams are stacked at 5-5. Wednesday's wire saw the Slumlords grab two free-agent quarterbacks in the same minute and LAB spend $6 in claims. ATL, CLE, GB, LAR, NE and SEA are all off in the biggest bye week of the year.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: eight straight after an 0-2 start, and the new quarterback skipped the warm-up. Brock Purdy dropped 55 in his first week, Cedric Gray's 39 led a 140 defense, and the Eddies beat LAB 272–198 to sit alone in first at 8-2, still on the bus with $25 left. Wednesday they grabbed Michael Mayer off free agency. Junk: Kyle Hamilton scored 23 on the bench while George Pickens dropped 49 for Ultron, so that trade is losing on the scoreboard for now. Next is a trip to the SPD's, freshly bounced off the bus and starting Bo Nix.

Juice: 298, the second-best score of the week, and Patrick Mahomes posted 50 three weeks after his 4. The Goats are 7-3, a game out of first, with the stingiest PA in the WU at 2207, and Wednesday added Nohl Williams for $2 and Nik Bonitto off free agency, leaving $16. Junk: this is a team playing for the standings, not the bus, Tank Dell's $26 debut was 5 points, and 2380.5 PF ranks eighth. Kevin Byard and Quincy Williams are on byes for a trip to Pocket, the WU's points leader.

Juice: alive on two fronts. Substation beat the Dongers 294–289.5 and LAB on Last Ride, so Substation gets a Week 11 shot back on the bus. Kaden Elliss' 47 was the best IDP score of the week, and the trade haul cashed in: Trevor Lawrence 37, Carson Schwesinger 32, Cameron Skattebo 28. Wednesday brought Jaelan Phillips for $1, plus Makai Lemon and David Njoku. Junk: $4 left, 2363.5 PF ranks 10th, and Schwesinger is on the Browns' bye for the trip to Saltese, the team that sent him over.

Juice: 341.5! Christian McCaffrey's 65 was the top player score in the WU, and the 162-point win over Saltese broke the season record. Doubtpfizer took the kitty, is 5-5 on two straight with a seat on the bus, sits second in PF at 2588.5, and still has the fattest wallet at $68 after $1 each on Jalen Carter and TreVeyon Henderson. Two titles in three years, and they're playing like it. Junk: Henderson is on the Patriots' bye, and 2591 PA is the second-worst in the WU. LAB visits with nothing left to lose.

Juice: still the WU's points leader at 2676 PF, 87.5 clear of Doubtpfizer, still on the bus, and $66 is the second-fattest wallet. Jared Goff's 36 and Tony Adams' 25 showed up. Junk: four straight losses, the latest 262.5–230 to TTAB, and the points leader also owns the worst PA in the WU at 2622.5. Tetairoa McMillan scored 6, and Ernest Jones is on the Seahawks' bye. The 7-3 Goats visit with the stingiest PA in the league.

Juice: still on the bus at 5-5 with 2542 PF, fourth in the WU. Emmett Johnson scored 44, and Wednesday Hyper spent $3 on Kaleb Elarms-Orr and $1 on Shaun Dolac, who's on the Rams' bye, leaving $13. Junk: Ultron beat them 265–221 with Hyper's own players, as Amon-Ra St. Brown, Nick Bolton and Kirk Cousins put up 74 while Josh Allen and Drake London gave back 44. The bus margin was 20, and London is on the Falcons' bye. TTAB visits with Bryce Young, Hyper's $7 flip, on the bench.

Juice: two straight, now 5-5, and they beat Hyper with Hyper's players: St. Brown 31, Bolton 25, Cousins 18. George Pickens, fresh from the Eddies, dropped 49, and Wednesday's $0 claims brought in Courtland Sutton and Jeremy Reaves. Junk: Myles Garrett scored 0, 128.5 points sat on the bench, the wallet is empty, and 2279 PF ranks 12th. Bijan Robinson, DeMarcco Hellams and Garrett are all on byes. The good news is the schedule: a trip to Morningside, losers of six straight.

Juice: TTAB beat the WU's points leader on defense alone. Quinnen Williams' 36 and Patrick Queen's 35 built a 170 IDP, best in the WU by 20, in a 262.5–230 win that got them to 5-5, and Caleb Williams is back from bye. Wednesday they swapped Andrew Wingard for Michael Taaffe. Junk: the offense scored 92.5, Bryce Young, the $7 trade bridge, scored 8, $3 is left, and 2311 PF ranks 11th. Next is a trip to Hyper, the team that sold them Young.

Juice: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 52, Maxx Crosby 40 and James Cook 35, and 2464 PF still ranks fifth in the WU. Junk: Drake Maye scored 2 in a 298–255.5 loss to the Goats, and with Maye on the Patriots' bye and $0 in the wallet, Wednesday turned into a free-agent quarterback scramble: Cam Ward and Jacoby Brissett at 9:05 AM, then Gunnar Helm and Josh Cameron, with Alex Anzalone cut. Devon Witherspoon is off with Seattle too. The Dongers visit, still mad about scoring 289.5 and losing.

Juice: they won, 201–194.5 over Morningside, and the defense did all of it, with Roquan Smith scoring 22 in his SPD's debut. Wednesday they paid $4 for Danny Stutsman and cut Xavier Watts, leaving $40. Junk: 201 was the lowest of the five alive, so the SPD's won their game and got thrown off the bus on the same scoreboard. The offense scored 66, lowest in the WU. Jordan Love and A.J. Brown are both on byes, so Bo Nix starts, and the 8-2 Eddies come to town.

Juice: Isaiah Likely's 45 was the top tight end score of the week, and $44 is still the third-fattest wallet after $4 on Dee Winters and $2 on Austin Booker. Junk: a 272–198 loss to the Eddies made it four straight after a 5-1 start, and Substation beat them on Last Ride, so LAB is off the bus for good. Nathan Landman scored 2 the week after LAB traded Roquan Smith for him, and Marcus Jones got cut a week after his $6 signing. Matthew Stafford is on bye for the trip to Doubtpfizer, fresh off 341.5.

Juice: 289.5, the most points in a loss all season, and enough to beat 10 of the other 13 teams. Joe Burrow's 52 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 43 led a 188.5 offense. Junk: they lost to Substation by 4.5 with Jevon Holland's 13 on the bench and Jalen Ramsey starting for 8, so the three-game streak is dead at 3-7, with $1 left. Smith-Njigba, Xavier McKinney, Christian Elliss and Isaiah McDuffie are all on byes for a trip to the Slumlords, who now have three quarterbacks.

Juice: Eric Wilson scored 30 in his first week after the Substation trade, and C.J. Stroud is finally the starting quarterback after Monday's Aaron Rodgers cleanup. Wednesday added M.J. Stewart for $1, Jonathan Allen and Dalton Schultz for $0, and Ashton Dulin off free agency, leaving $2. Junk: 179.5 was the week's floor for the second straight week, and the 162-point loss to Doubtpfizer was the biggest margin of the season. Rodgers started for 19 while Stroud scored 25 on the bench. Substation visits with Schwesinger in its colors.

Juice: they lost by only 6.5, Daiyan Henley scored 30, and Wednesday $1 swapped Keenan Allen for Elic Ayomanor, leaving $6. Junk: Xavier Worthy started and scored 0 while Deebo Samuel scored 35 on the bench, in that 6.5-point loss. That's six straight, the longest active skid in the WU, and dead last in PF at 2050.5, 201 behind 13th. Drew Lock is on the Seahawks' bye, and he's still the only quarterback on the roster after waivers cleared. Ultron visits on two straight wins.
